claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during rapid solidification.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence during thermal treatment.
A 2–5 T static magnetic field applied during rapid solidification will align magnetic moments associated with Fe, Co, and Ni in the melt.
Magnetic-moment alignment will disrupt the short-range atomic order required for crystal nucleation.
The applied magnetic field will modify magnetic ordering and interfere with embryonic crystalline-cluster formation in the melt.
Disruption of short-range order will increase the critical free-energy barrier for crystallite formation.
An increased nucleation barrier will delay or suppress nucleation during cooling.
Suppressed nucleation during cooling will increase amorphous retention.
Magnetic-field-assisted solidification will improve the thermal stability of the retained amorphous phase during reheating.
Magnetic-field-processed samples will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than samples processed without the field.
Magnetic-field-processed samples will exhibit reduced or shifted exothermic crystallization peaks.
Magnetic-field-processed samples will exhibit an enlarged supercooled-liquid region.
The baseline alloy exhibits multiple intense crystallization events on reheating after rapid cooling.
The baseline alloy has a narrow supercooled-liquid region and limited amorphous retention.
The proposed effect is specifically effective at cooling rates above 10^5 K/s, magnetic-field strengths of 2–5 T, and reheating rates near 20 K/min.
Conditions outside the stated cooling-rate, magnetic-field, or reheating-rate boundaries may reduce suppression of nucleation and amorphous retention.
